findings.title: Excessive Gateway Intents requesting all intents
findings.description: The bot client is initialized with Object.values(GatewayIntentBits), which requests ALL gateway intents including privileged ones (GuildMembers, GuildPresences, MessageContent). This violates the principle of least privilege and exposes the bot to receiving far more data than necessary, increasing the attack surface if the bot token is compromised.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly list only the required intents: Guilds, GuildMembers, GuildVoiceStates, GuildMessageReactions, GuildMessages, MessageContent. Remove the blanket Object.values() call.

findings.title: Unsafe JSON.parse of user-controlled button customId
findings.description: In src/index.ts lines 115 and 136, the bot calls JSON.parse(customId) on button and modal submit interaction customIds. While Discord limits customId to 100 characters and the values originate from bot-created buttons, a malicious client or modified Discord client could craft arbitrary JSON in the customId field, leading to unexpected action routing or prototype pollution via crafted JSON payloads.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try-catch with validation. Validate that the parsed object contains only expected fields (action, value) and that 'action' is a known registered action name before dispatching.

findings.title: Missing authorization check on /ticket command
findings.description: The /ticket command creates categories with restricted permissions (moderator-only) but has no permission check on who can execute the command. The code has a comment '// 認証関連をここに実装。実行できる人は限られる想定' (implement auth here, limited users expected) but no actual authorization logic. Any guild member can create ticket categories and boards.
findings.recommendation: Add a permission check verifying the interaction member has the moderator or admin role (from botConfig.role) before allowing category creation. Use interaction.memberPermissions or check role IDs.

findings.title: Hardcoded Discord IDs expose internal server structure
findings.description: Multiple files contain hardcoded Discord snowflake IDs: bot.config.ts (role IDs, channel IDs, category IDs), src/index.ts (role IDs on lines 172-183, 202-215), src/jobs/updateMemberCount.ts (CHANNEL_ID, GUILD_ID), src/jobs/noticeNewRecruit.ts (channel ID). These expose the internal server structure and make the code inflexible. If committed to a public repository, attackers can enumerate the Discord server's structure.
findings.recommendation: Move all Discord IDs to environment variables or a configuration file that is excluded from version control. Use .env for all server-specific IDs.

findings.title: Webhook URL used in error handler may leak to logs
findings.description: In src/handlers/events/vc/leave.ts, the error handler sends error details to a webhook URL from process.env.WEBHOOK_URL. The error object is interpolated directly into the webhook message body as a string, which could leak internal stack traces, file paths, and server details to wherever the webhook points. Additionally, WEBHOOK_URL is not listed in .env.example, suggesting it may be undefined in some environments.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize the error message before sending to the webhook. Only send a generic error indicator, not the full error object. Add WEBHOOK_URL to .env.example. Handle the case where WEBHOOK_URL is undefined (currently falls through to fetch with empty string URL).

findings.title: Race condition in voice channel cleanup
findings.description: In src/handlers/events/vc/leave.ts, the check for channel.members.size === 0 and subsequent channel.delete() is not atomic. Between the size check and the delete call, another user could join the channel, leading to deletion of an occupied channel. Similarly in join.ts, the channel creation and user move are separate operations with no rollback.
findings.recommendation: Re-fetch the channel state before deletion to verify it is still empty. Implement a locking mechanism or use a debounce/delay before deletion to handle rapid join/leave events. Add error handling that checks if the channel still exists before deleting.

findings.title: Ticket channel inherits only user permissions, missing deny for @everyone
findings.description: In src/handlers/button/ticket.ts, when creating a ticket channel (line 31-41), only the requesting user gets explicit ViewChannel/SendMessages permissions. The channel inherits from its parent category, but there is no explicit deny for @everyone on the ticket channel itself. If the category permissions are modified later, tickets could become visible to all members.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit permissionOverwrite denying ViewChannel for interaction.guild.roles.everyone when creating ticket channels, similar to how the parent category is configured.

findings.title: No rate limiting or duplicate ticket prevention
findings.description: The ticket-open button handler creates a new channel every time it is clicked. There is no check for existing open tickets by the same user, no cooldown, and no limit on the number of tickets. A user could spam the button to create hundreds of channels, exhausting the 500-channel limit per Discord guild (denial of service).
findings.recommendation: Check if the user already has an open ticket channel before creating a new one. Implement a cooldown or rate limit. Consider adding a maximum ticket count per user.

findings.title: ManageChannels permission granted to VC room creator
findings.description: In src/handlers/events/vc/join.ts, the user who triggers custom VC creation is granted ManageChannels permission on their room. This allows the user to modify the channel in unintended ways - renaming it, changing bitrate, region, user limits, or modifying permissions to grant/deny access to arbitrary users, potentially bypassing server moderation.
findings.recommendation: Remove ManageChannels from user permissions. If the intent is to let users customize their room name, implement a bot command that validates the new name instead of granting broad channel management permissions.

findings.title: User-controlled input in channel name without sanitization
findings.description: In src/handlers/events/vc/join.ts line 12, the username is directly interpolated into the channel name without sanitization. Discord usernames can contain special characters. While Discord's API limits channel names, the lack of sanitization could lead to confusing or misleading channel names.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize the username before using it in the channel name. Strip or replace special characters and enforce a maximum length.

findings.title: CI/CD deploy workflow uses self-hosted runner with tag injection risk
findings.description: The deploy.yml workflow runs on a self-hosted runner and uses github.event.release.tag_name directly in a git checkout command. While the tag must exist to trigger the release event, a tag name containing shell metacharacters could be exploited for command injection on the self-hosted runner. The workflow also reveals the server filesystem path (/home/sora81dev/discord-bot/nanase-bot).
findings.recommendation: Sanitize or validate the tag name format before use in shell commands. Use environment variables instead of direct interpolation: env: TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }} then reference $TAG. Avoid exposing server paths in public repositories.

findings.title: Docker container runs as root
findings.description: The Dockerfile does not specify a USER directive, meaning the bot runs as root inside the container. If the bot or a dependency has a vulnerability allowing code execution, the attacker would have root privileges inside the container.
findings.recommendation: Add a non-root user in the Dockerfile: RUN adduser --disabled-password botuser && USER botuser. Also add a WORKDIR directive.

findings.title: No WORKDIR set in Dockerfile, files copied to root filesystem
findings.description: The Dockerfile copies package.json and source files to the container root (/) without setting WORKDIR. This mixes application files with system files and could lead to unintended file overwrites.
findings.recommendation: Add WORKDIR /app before COPY commands.

findings.title: Non-null assertion operators on environment variables
findings.description: Multiple files use the non-null assertion operator (!) on process.env values (e.g., process.env['NOTIFIER_ROLE_ID']! in addReactionRole.ts, removeReactionRole.ts; process.env['REACTIONROLE_CHANNEL_ID']! in checkReactionRoleMessage.ts). If these environment variables are not set, the values will be undefined, causing silent failures or runtime errors when used as Discord API arguments.
findings.recommendation: Validate all required environment variables at startup. Throw a descriptive error if any are missing rather than using non-null assertions.

findings.title: Duplicate role assignment in guildMemberAdd handler
findings.description: In src/index.ts lines 172-175, when a bot joins, the same role ID '1454099602641780737' is added twice - once labeled as 'BOT role' and once as 'student role'. This is likely a copy-paste bug. Bots should not receive the student role.
findings.recommendation: Fix the second roles.add call to use the correct student role ID, or remove it if bots should not get the student role.

findings.title: Reaction role system has no bot-user exclusion
findings.description: The messageReactionAdd and messageReactionRemove handlers in index.ts do not check if the reacting user is a bot. If another bot reacts to the reaction role message, it could trigger unintended role assignments.
findings.recommendation: Add a check at the beginning of the reaction handlers: if (user.bot) return;

findings.title: Production uses ts-node dev runner instead of compiled JavaScript
findings.description: The docker-compose.yml runs 'npm run dev' which uses ts-node to run TypeScript directly. This is less performant and not recommended for production. The build/start scripts exist but are not used in the Docker configuration.
findings.recommendation: Use a multi-stage Docker build: compile TypeScript in a build stage, then copy the compiled JS to a production image and run with 'npm start'.

findings.title: .gitignore uses incorrect node_modules path
findings.description: The .gitignore file lists '/node_packages/' on line 1 instead of '/node_modules/'. While node_modules/ is correctly listed on line 81 from the generated template, the custom entry appears to be a typo that serves no purpose.
findings.recommendation: Change '/node_packages/' to '/node_modules/' or remove the duplicate entry since node_modules/ is already listed.

findings.title: Error messages logged to console may contain sensitive data
findings.description: Throughout the codebase, full error objects are logged via console.error(error). In a production environment, these logs could contain sensitive information such as Discord API tokens in request headers, user data, or internal state.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured logging that sanitizes sensitive fields. Avoid logging full error objects in production.

findings.title: Server filesystem path disclosed in deploy workflow
findings.description: The deploy.yml workflow reveals the absolute server path '/home/sora81dev/discord-bot/nanase-bot' and the username 'sora81dev'. This information disclosure aids attackers in targeting the deployment server.
findings.recommendation: Use a deploy action or script that does not hardcode the server path. Reference paths via environment variables or secrets.
